Lift + Cruise VTOL Review

Hybrid VTOL with vertical lift rotors for takeoff and landing, and a pusher prop and fixed wing for cruise. Student capstone.

1 · Overview

Overview

Baseline: C0, a 4-lift twin-boom quadplane built to a fixed $2,000 cap. It has a 2.4 m span and a m² NACA 2415 wing (AR , chord mm). Lift comes from four SunnySky X4110S motors on 17-in props, and a fifth X4110S drives a 14×8.5 pusher. The aircraft has 6061 aluminium booms and spar on a taped XPS foam wing, and runs ArduPilot QuadPlane on a CoreWing F405 Wing board. Sized MTOW is kg, with hover thrust-to-weight . It hovers on W and cruises at 20 m/s on W. On one 6S 6500 mAh pack it has min of cruise after the hover allowance and 20 % reserve. Verdict: it closes physically and financially. Committed spend including tax and shipping is , which leaves a crash reserve under the cap. That reserve is thin (decision below).

What changed from v0.2

v0.2 used a Pixhawk avionics set, X6 SE lift units, carbon tubes and a glass-epoxy wing. Its all-in cost was , so it failed the cap. The team confirmed that $2,000 is fixed and covers everything physical, tax and shipping included. v0.3 keeps the architecture and changes every high-cost part:

Areav0.2 goodsv0.3 goodsSaving

analysis/results_v0.2_baseline.json vs analysis/results.json, category totals of the C0 BOM (goods, pre-tax)

v0.3.1 (same day): a six-reviewer project audit (§12) confirmed 79 findings. The design changes it drove:

  • booms moved outboard so the pusher disc clears the rear lift discs (it overlapped by 30 mm)
  • joiner lengthened to 0.76 m, for 0.30 m of engagement per side
  • wing thickened to NACA 2415, with the spar at 30 % chord, for foam cover over the socket
  • fifth servo for twin rudders
  • motor mounts moved to PA6-CF
  • previously missing wiring, glue, battery straps and a hot-wire allowance added
  • transition speed raised to 16 m/s (R11)

Open decisions

Which legal path and which flying field? Flight testing can't be scheduled until this is settled.
The campus policy permits "University of California courses (including senior projects)", which covers the capstone. Site limits:
  • Richmond Field Station: 400 ft AGL
  • Clark Kerr track: 200 ft AGL
  • La Loma field: below 20 ft, inside the fences
  • All sites: 6 a.m. to sunset; no flying on game or graduation days
Each flight needs a request filed ≥ 7 business days ahead and ≥ $1M liability cover per pilot. A transition needs ≥ 30 m AGL and 50–100 m of straight flight. That rules out La Loma, limits Clark Kerr to hover and low passes, and leaves Richmond Field Station as the only campus site for transitions.
Recommended: by 2026-11-06, request Richmond Field Station from UCPD/Risk Services. Confirm the capstone's institutional sponsorship, which the § 350 educational path implies. Each pilot holds TRUST and AMA Full ($89, outside the cap). Alternative: one member passes Part 107 ($175) and the team flies at an off-campus field.

R18, R19; oercs.berkeley.edu/policies/campus-policy-library/unmanned-aircraft-system-drone-policy (site limits and senior-project clause, checked 2026-10-13) · §11

The crash reserve is thin: against a $100 floor.
v0.3.1 added items the audit found missing: wiring, glue, battery straps, a fifth servo, PA6-CF mounts and a hot-wire allowance. These are estimates, and several small items are still unpriced: charger adapter, motor bullets, prop adapters and Holybro duty (—).
Recommended: borrow a hot-wire cutter from a campus makerspace, which frees $44. Build the carts early and re-check against the $100 shipping allowance. Alternatives, in order: drop the spare motor ($52 with tax), then the airspeed sensor ($66; R11 then needs Q_ASSIST_SPEED 11 m/s and synthetic airspeed).

analysis/results.json C0.bom; §7

The flight controller's ArduPilot target is beta-only today.
The CoreWing F405 Wing APP V2 ($67.26, 12 outputs, 90 A current sensor, 8 A servo BEC) has a firmware target only in Plane 4.7.2-beta. Every F405 build includes QuadPlane but drops OctaQuad, Lua and DLVR airspeed.
Recommended: buy the CoreWing and bench-test on 4.7.2-beta in SITL and on the bench. Hold a go/no-go on 2027-02-22: if no stable target exists by then, move to the Matek F405-WMO ($69.99, stable). The Matek has 9–10 outputs, so with 10 needed (5 servos, pusher, 4 lift) both rudders go on a Y-lead. Alternative: buy the Matek now.

docs/research/budget-avionics.md §0–§2 · §10

Accept no hover motor-out tolerance (R14)?
C0 cannot hold attitude after losing a lift motor in hover. The 8-lift (C1) keeps T/W after a motor-out, but its spend is , which is over the cap.
Recommended: accept for C0. Keep hovers under 5 m AGL and under 60 s each, and qualify every motor on the thrust stand first. Alternative: none fits under $2,000.

R14; analysis/results.json · §3

How do the stopped lift props sit in cruise?
BLHeli_S ESCs cannot stop a prop at a set angle, so a 2-blade prop stops wherever it lands. Folding props add $14–16 per station.
Recommended: run the car-roof test (§3 M1) on one stopped unit at 20 m/s. If the prop windmills or sits crosswise, print a stop pawl. Alternative: Eolo folding 17×6.2, $49.99 a pair. Two pairs cost $99.98, about $110 with tax, and that exceeds the reserve.

docs/research/budget-lift.md caveat 4; Props table (folding) · §3

MTOW lands at kg, under the 8–15 kg working target.
The 8–15 kg range was a working target, not a hard limit; the hard cap is 25 kg. The cost cap and the short mission drive mass down. A smaller aircraft is cheaper, easier to carry (R5) and safer to test.
Recommended: accept, and record it in the design basis as pending team sign-off. Alternative: add payload or ballast to reach 8 kg. That needs more battery, motor and money and buys nothing.

R2; docs/DESIGN-BASIS.md v0.3.1 · §4

2 · CAD model

CAD model

The SOLIDWORKS model is generated from the sizing outputs by cad/build.ps1. Re-running the sizing and the build regenerates every part, so the CAD can't drift from the numbers. It has 25 parts in a 46-component assembly:

  • NACA 2415 wing panels with 26 % chord ailerons and a spar socket bored at 30 % chord
  • NACA 0009 tailplane seated on the booms, with an elevator fitted between lofted, tapered fins
  • turned motors, pusher spinner and pitot
  • tapered two-blade props, shown parked fore-aft (notional: BLHeli_S ESCs cannot park them)
  • printed boom clamps whose tops meet the wing surface at each station
  • PA6-CF motor mounts
  • gear clamps with legs and feet

params.mjs checks the pusher-to-lift-disc clearance, currently mm (minimum 20 mm). Parts are placed by coordinates, not mates, and SOLIDWORKS interference detection has not been run, so interfaces are visual (—).

What the team must measure

  1. M1
    Built component masses. Kitchen scale (5 kg, 1 g) on each piece as it comes off the bench, logged against the parts table. If the empty mass, without battery and payload, exceeds kg + 15 %, re-run the sizing. T/W falls toward R13 and cruise time below the 25 % margin.
  2. M2
    Car load space. Tape-measure the boot of the team's actual car. A clear length under m fails R4.
  3. M3
    Assembly time. Stopwatch two people from car to armed pre-flight, three runs. A median over 15 min fails R5.
3 · Concepts

Concepts

C0 (4-lift) is the only layout that fits the cap with a useful reserve. With budget parts, the 8-lift (C1) is over the cap by . The coaxial X8 (C2) is over by , partly because OctaQuad needs an H7 board. C3 is C0 with X3515S motors. Its spend is , about $15 less, but it hovers on W against W. Motor heat is the tighter constraint (§12), so C0 stays.

What the team must measure

  1. M1
    Stopped-prop attitude. Car-roof mast, one motor and prop unpowered, 20 m/s on a closed lot; film the prop. Windmilling, or a stop more than 30° off the airflow, adds drag beyond the R10 estimate. Fit a stop pawl, or folding props ($110 with tax).
4 · Mass & power

Mass & power

MTOW is the output of an energy-closed loop. Mission energy sets battery mass, mass sets wing area and hover power, and those feed back into the energy. With a continuous battery the loop closes at kg, needing Wh. The real pack chosen is the cheapest one that keeps ≥ 11.5 min of cruise, a 15 % design margin est over R10, on top of its 20 % energy reserve. It is the ( Wh), giving MTOW kg.

What the team must measure

  1. M1
    Hover electrical power at full weight. Watt meter in a 30 s tethered hover, or one motor on the thrust stand at g. Above W, R10 fails on the selected pack. The maker-data estimate is W.
  2. M2
    Parasite drag. Log cruise current at 20 m/s in still air and back out drag with F7. Above W cruise power (total CD0 above , against estimated), R10 fails on the selected pack.
  3. M3
    Stopped-rotor drag. Car-roof mast with a luggage scale on a pivot, 20 m/s. The model assumes N per stopped unit at 20 m/s. Above about N per unit, R10 fails on the selected pack.
  4. M4
    Pack usable energy. Discharge at about 16 A (cruise current) on the charger, logging Wh. Under Wh delivered, the 20 % reserve of R10 fails.
5 · Propulsion

Propulsion

Lift: SunnySky X4110S 400KV on 17-in props with SoloGood 45 A BLHeli_S ESCs, $66.29 per station. Max thrust is 3.13 kgf, for T/W . At C0's hover thrust each motor draws W. The pusher is a fifth X4110S on an APC 14×8.5EP, so one spare motor covers every position. Energy comes from two Ovonic 6S 6500 mAh LiPos ($138.99 for the 2-pack listing) and an HTRC C150 charger. The packs ship with EC5 leads; re-terminate them to the kit's XT90-S anti-spark plugs, which are also the R20 physical disconnect.

What the team must measure

  1. M1
    Lift thrust curve on our pack. DIY stand (20 kg load cell + HX711 + Nano, calibrated with water jugs), watt meter in line, five throttle steps. Max under 2.4 kgf fails R13 (4 × 2.4 kgf / kg ≈ 1.6).
  2. M2
    Motor heat in a mission-length hover. Hold g for 90 s, read the can with the IR thermometer every 15 s, and let it cool below 45 °C before the next run. A mission has one hover of about 80 s at each end, with about 10 min of cruise cooling between. A can over 80 °C est after one 90 s run fails R9 hover duty (the lumped model predicts °C). Never fly back-to-back hovers: three 90 s runs with 30 s rests reach about °C in the model. The PA6-CF mounts tolerate the base temperature; PETG mounts would not (HDT about 68 °C).
  3. M3
    Pusher current and static thrust on 14×8.5EP. Thrust stand + watt meter. Static thrust under 1.5 kgf at 60 % throttle, or a peak over 40 A, means dropping to a 13×8 prop.
  4. M4
    Pack sag at hover current. Watt meter on all four lift motors at hover throttle, tied down. Also run a 3 s full-throttle burst on all four lift motors. Below 3.4 V/cell est at hover current, or below 3.2 V/cell in the burst, fails R13 margin. Move to the 8000 mAh pack (+$61, which exceeds the reserve).
6 · Structures

Structures

The 6061-T6 wing joiner is the critical member. At ultimate load (4.5 g) the hand calc on the true 0.875 in joiner gives MPa, a reserve factor of on yield. That figure governs. The FEA models the joiner bonded inside the socket (OD = socket ID) and gives MPa on a 2 mm mesh, so it confirms the load path under that idealisation. Booms are strength-rich: MPa on a 1.5 mm mesh, with mm tip deflection at full thrust. Landing gear needs a compliant element with about 100 mm of travel if it behaves like a spring.

The X4110S no-load speed is 400 KV × 22.2 V = 8,880 rpm (148 Hz). Hover speed is not in the published table (—). If it lands near a multiple of Hz the booms will resonate; the tap test (M2) settles it.

Landing loads

Gear stroke, mmDamped n = 1 + h/sSpring n = 2(1 + h/s)Verdict (spring bound)

Energy balance, drop h = 0.30 m est. Bare aluminium legs act as springs, so read the right-hand column. A foam or TPU foot with about 100 mm of travel keeps n ≤ 8.

Joints and materials

  • Wing–fuselage: 0.6 m aluminium joiner through the pod into the sockets, plus one M5 bolt per half at the trailing-edge rib for incidence and anti-rotation est.
  • Boom–wing: two printed PETG clamps per boom, seated on the wing lower surface (CAD §2), plus one M4 through-bolt per clamp to stop the boom rotating under differential thrust est. Typical PETG HDT is 68 °C (Prusament datasheet); the purchased ELEGOO PETG has no published HDT (—).
  • Motor mounts: printed PA6-CF20 saddles (HDT 173 °C, Polymaker datasheet). The lumped thermal model puts the motor near °C after a 90 s hover, too close to PETG's limit.
  • Wing: hot-wire FOAMULAR XPS core with packing-tape skin. σ_wing = kg/m² by F11. Tape mass per area is not published, so it is estimated est (M4).

docs/research/budget-airframe.md §1–§5

What the team must measure

  1. M1
    Wing proof load. Invert the wing on pod-width supports and sandbag it to limit load (3.0 × W), hold 30 s. Any permanent set in the joiner, or tip deflection over 10 % of semi-span, fails the wing for flight.
  2. M2
    Boom natural frequency. Tap the motor and record with a phone spectrum app. Within ±15 % of the hover rotor frequency (or twice it), add a strut before flight.
  3. M3
    Gear stroke. Drop the empty airframe 0.3 m onto grass; read peak g from the flight-controller log. Over 8 g, fit softer feet before the hover test.
  4. M4
    Tape skin mass. Weigh a 0.5 m² taped foam sample against bare foam. Over 0.1 kg/m² per side, update F11 and re-run the sizing (R2, R10).
  5. M5
    Boom clamp proof load. Hang 1.5 × T_max ( N) from the front motor station with the rear free, and check for slip or rotation at the clamps. Any rotation over 1° or any crack fails the boom joint (R9).

Cost risks

  • Shipping above the allowance. OnlineMetals ships 72–96 in tube by UPS, priced only at checkout (M2).
  • A crash. A wing half plus a motor and props is about $120 in parts est, which is more than the reserve. Spare foam, tube offcuts and a spare motor and props are already in the BOM, so a typical crash needs only consumables.
  • China-shipped items: the Holybro airspeed sensor, and possibly the ESCs. Allow for duty and longer lead time.
  • Prices are single snapshots from 2026-10-13. Re-check them before ordering.

What the team must confirm

  1. M1
    Cart totals before ordering. Build each vendor cart to the shipping page without paying. If any cart pushes the reserve under $100 (R7), borrow a hot-wire cutter first ($44), then drop the spare motor ($52), then the airspeed sensor ($66).
  2. M2
    OnlineMetals UPS quote for 2 × 72 in + 96 in + 36 in tube. Over $40 means buying the joiner tube locally.
8 · Testing & failure

Testing & failure

Weakest link: a lift-motor or ESC failure in hover. C0 has no recovery from it. Next are a hard landing on stiff gear and an unproven BLHeli_S ESC under sustained hover current. The $69 test and safety kit (LiPo bag, ammo can, load cell, Nano, watt meter, IR thermometer) qualifies every motor and ESC before flight. The flight build-up is in §13.

9 · CG & stability

CG & stability

The CG target is 28 % MAC, and the lift thrust centroid is placed on it by construction. Static margin is % with the payload allowance and % without it. The vortex-lattice model independently puts the neutral point at % MAC, against % from the tail-volume formula. Without the payload the CG moves aft and the rear rotors carry % more thrust, so carry ballast in the payload bay.

analysis/sizing.mjs cg(), geometry(); analysis/vlm.mjs → aero.json; fuselage destabilising term not included in either

What the team must measure

  1. M1
    Actual CG. Two kitchen scales under the wing at known stations. Aft of % MAC (SM under 8 % est) fails cruise stability. Fly without the payload only with ballast in the bay, and move the battery to bring the CG within 2 cm of the thrust centroid.
  2. M2
    Hover pitch trim. Front vs rear motor outputs in a 30 s hover log. A split over 15 % means the CG is off the thrust centroid by more than about cm, which eats hover control margin (R13).
10 · Controls

Controls

ArduPilot Plane QuadPlane on a CoreWing F405 Wing APP V2. The board has 12 outputs (10 used), a 90 A current sensor and an 8 A servo BEC set to 6 V for the five ES3005HV servos. Transition completes at AIRSPEED_MIN = 16 m/s, which meets R11's 1.3 × stall, measured by the MS5525 airspeed sensor. Lift motors taper out over 5 s, and Q_ASSIST_SPEED is 13 m/s. Telemetry runs over ELRS MAVLink, so no separate radio is needed.

12 · Simulation & verification

Simulation & verification

Every SOLIDWORKS Simulation result agrees with its hand calculation within 15 %, and every margin passes. Each FEA model uses the same idealisation as its hand calc (rigid root, bonded joiner), so the FEA confirms the hand calcs rather than independently validating them. Clamp compliance would lower the boom frequency. The studies are FEA of the boom and the spar/joiner, a boom modal study and a lift-motor thermal study. A vortex-lattice model confirms the neutral point and the lift slope. An independent Python check re-derives every sizing formula and the BOM. Aerodynamic CFD was not run because SOLIDWORKS Flow Simulation would not load on this licence.

cad/Sim.cs → cad/sim/results.txt and *.SLDPRT (studies inside); analysis/vlm.mjs → aero.json; analysis/verify.py

Results against hand calcs

StudyQuantityFEA / modelHand / sizingDiffMargin

SOLIDWORKS 2025 Simulation (Educational licence, watermark on plots). Linear static, 2nd-order tets ≈ 3 mm; 6061-T6 (SS) library material. Simplified load-path models: boom arm cantilevered at the spar clamp with a tip block sized to the lift-unit mass (motor + ESC + prop + mount, kg); spar + joiner half-span fixed at the centreline, carrying a uniform load scaled to the elliptic root moment.

Motor heat: steady FEA and 90 s hover

Heat into each lift motor is estimated at 20 % of the hover input ( W) est, with prop-wash convection at 50 W/m²K est and 35 °C ambient. Steady-state FEA gives °C, a bulk-temperature estimate for unlimited hover. Hover lasts 60–90 s, so the time response decides. The lumped estimate for a 90 s hover is °C (band °C for c = 385–500 J/kgK; time constant s). Three back-to-back 90 s runs with 30 s rests would reach about °C, so T3 cools the motor to 45 °C between runs.

Transient thermal through the Simulation API returned no saved time steps (tested 2026-10-13), so the 90 s value is lumped capacitance. Motor heat capacity uses a mass-weighted c of 470 J/kgK est. Copper (385) and steel (460) have lower c than aluminium (896), so an all-aluminium assumption would understate the temperature rise.

Aerodynamics: vortex lattice

QuantityVLMSizing estimateComment

analysis/vlm.mjs: horseshoe vortices, wing 48 × 4 + tail 16 × 2 panels, cosine spanwise spacing (Katz & Plotkin, Low-Speed Aerodynamics, ch. 12). Inviscid; stopped rotors, booms and fuselage excluded.

Run CFD for stopped-rotor drag if Flow Simulation can be licensed.
Stopped-rotor and boom drag (ΣCdA) is the largest unmeasured term in cruise power. Flow Simulation is installed but would not start through the API, and the licence lists only the base SOLIDWORKS serial.
Recommended: ask the department whether the SOLIDWORKS Education licence includes Flow Simulation. If it does, re-run with an external-flow project at 20 m/s on cad/model/VTOL_Concept.SLDASM. Alternative: the car-roof drag test (§4 M3) measures the same term directly.

What the team must measure

  1. M1
    FEA boundary check. Dial gauge or ruler on the boom tip with the measured clamp, under a known hanging weight. Deflection over 1.5 × the FEA value means clamp compliance dominates. Re-run the boom modal study with the measured stiffness before transition tests (R9).
  2. M2
    Motor temperature curve. IR thermometer every 15 s during T3. A measured time constant under 100 s, or a 90 s value over 80 °C, invalidates the lumped model and the hover limits (R9).
13 · Flight test & operations

Flight test & operations

Fly a strict build-up: SITL, bench, tethered hover, free hover, Q-mode handling, partial transitions, full transition, then the mission. Each step has entry, abort and success criteria. C0 has no hover motor-out tolerance and runs beta firmware, so the early steps stay low and short.

Crew, field procedure and charging

  • Crew roles: pilot in command (TRUST holder), visual observer, ground-station operator, and safety officer with the fire bag and extinguisher. Names: —.
  • Before each flight: props checked; CG checked; Remote ID broadcasting; geofence loaded; battery plugged in last through the XT90-S; area clear.
  • LiPo procedure: charge only in the LiPo bag inside the ammo can and never unattended. Inspect each pack for swelling and store at storage voltage. A crashed pack is isolated outdoors for 30 min.
  • Field charging cadence: the HTRC C150 gives about 6 A on 6S, roughly 1.1 h per 6500 mAh pack est. With two packs, a 2–3 h session supports about 3–4 flights. A field power source is needed (—).
